main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large sloped snow roof seen from above over a log-wall front with a door and two shuttered windows
top_band: Roof snow, light white-blue, rows ~8-31, with a darker blue-grey eave band at rows ~31-35 and icicles at rows 36-40
evidence: The middle column meets the snow roof slope as a tall light surface, then a darker eave band and a snowy front edge. Dark shadow and icicles follow at rows 36-40, then the log wall from rows 40-62. The roof reads as a top surface like the reference roofs. The door has a frame and the windows have shutters set into the logs, so the front is inset rather than flat.

style.evidence: The snow has about 4-5 steps (white, pale blue, mid blue, grey-blue shadow) with scalloped drift marks and icicles. The logs carry 4 browns with grain and snow caps, and the lit windows are well shaded. Outlines are dark brown and navy tints, not black. The roof has some wide pale areas with only sparse variation, so it is a little less dense than the references, but it stays in the same craft class and reads as a deliberate snow surface.
